This narrative review yields causal distinctions and evidence-boundary corrections, not a sufficiently supported new intervention hypothesis.

group_assessment.weighting: Europe PMC author counts measured 2026-08-10: Aqeilan RI 149 total and 79 with WWOX; Steinberg DJ 13 total and 7 with WWOX. This is a primary experimental WWOX/WOREE-model group with direct mouse, organoid and gene-restoration work. That raises confidence in model coverage and technical context, but the present article is a narrative review from the same group that produced several load-bearing primaries. Its observations and interpretations are weighted separately: it is authoritative synthesis, not independent replication.

field_density.note: The exact neuron-specific, organoid and myelin intersections are sparse. The review is therefore valuable as a map, but the small field and same-group dependence make primary-source boundaries and independent replication especially important. A fourth sequential ESearch request for a metabolic intersection returned HTTP 429 and was not substituted with a guessed count.

entries.proposition: The reviewed cell-targeted experiment included neural stem cells, mature neurons, astrocytes and oligodendrocyte-lineage cells.
entries.snippet: The targeted populations were neural stem cells (NSCs; Nestin-Cre; referred to as N-KO), neurons (Synapsin-I-Cre; S-KO), astrocytes (GFAP-Cre; G-KO), and oligodendrocytes and oligodendrocyte progenitors (Olig2-Cre; O-KO).

entries.proposition: Only Nestin- and Synapsin-targeted deletion were reported to recapitulate the null phenotype in the stated interval.
entries.snippet: Remarkably, at the reported time frame, only two models recapitulated the phenotype of the Wwox-null mice: the N-KO, in which WWOX was deleted in NSCs and its progenies, effectively knocking it out in all the cellular populations of the CNS. The second model was the S-KO in which WWOX is mutated only in mature neurons.

entries.proposition: The review attributes neurological and systemic null-like phenotypes to Nestin and mature-neuron deletion.
entries.snippet: It is important to emphasize that N-KO and S-KO recapitulated both neurological phenotypes (such as ataxia and seizures), but also systemic phenotypes such as growth retardation, metabolic abnormalities, and premature death by about 4-weeks of age.

entries.proposition: The review labels the neuron-to-oligodendrocyte myelin phenotype non-cell-autonomous.
entries.snippet: All the methods mentioned above led to the conclusion that ablation of neuronal-WWOX causes severe hypomyelination and decreased numbers of mature OLs in a noncell autonomous manner.
entries.anchor: Section 2.2, RNA-seq and oligodendrocyte validation paragraph

entries.proposition: The authors explicitly contrast a normal metabolic screen in one severe human case with rodent findings.
entries.snippet: Some very important observations were made – first, in contrast to the rodent data, the metabolic screen appeared normal.

entries.proposition: Early organoid WWOX expression was localized mainly to ventricular radial glia before broadening later.
entries.snippet: First, we stained for WWOX and were surprised to discover that during the early stages of organoids culture WWOX expression was limited to the vRGs.

entries.proposition: The organoid metabolic signal is transcriptomic pathway enrichment, not a flux measurement.
entries.snippet: GESA and GO terms analysis revealed many affected pathways, such as processes related to ATP synthesis coupled electron transport, oxidative phosphorylation, glycolysis and gluconeogenesis, and negative regulation of cell cycle.

entries.proposition: Diffuse organoid restoration was incomplete and motivated a cell-type-specific strategy.
entries.snippet: That being said, the phenotype was not rescued completely and included the uncontrolled expression of WWOX in all cellular populations, which made us speculate that a cell-type-specific approach would be more appropriate.

entries.proposition: The review reports that neuron-specific WWOX restoration rescues phenotypes measured outside the CNS.
entries.snippet: Furthermore, CNS neuronal-specific restoration of WWOX also rescued abnormalities in other tissues (bone and testis), as well as systemic symptoms such as hypoglycemia, growth retardation, and premature lethality.

entries.proposition: The authors acknowledge that no available model is complete and advocate model combination.
entries.snippet: Despite this, no model is currently perfect and major drawbacks can be found in all of them. Therefore, we believe the combination of these models can benefit both the scientific community in the mechanistic understanding of the disease, and patients in the development of new and safe treatments.
